title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space sector continues to stir, with AI models being tested for Earth observation and new partnerships forming around satellite intelligence. Meanwhile, the U.S. grapples with its response framework for hostile actions in space, while budget allocations hint at a growing focus on resilience.

themes.title: AI Takes to the Skies
themes.body: Loft Orbital's foray into AI for Earth observation could signal a shift in how data is collected and analyzed from space. As AI becomes more integral, expect a wave of startups to emerge, eager to capitalize on this trend.

themes.title: Partnerships in Space Intelligence
themes.body: Satellogic's collaboration with SynMax to develop services around the Merlin constellation highlights a growing trend of public-private partnerships in satellite intelligence. Such alliances may redefine the competitive landscape, as companies leverage shared resources and expertise.

themes.title: Space Resilience Funding Grows
themes.body: The recent $1.4 billion boost to the space resilience line in the FY27 budget reflects a heightened awareness of vulnerabilities in the space domain. This funding increase may fuel innovations in defense technologies, as companies seek to address emerging threats.

themes.title: Rocket Development on the Rise
themes.body: China's apparent development of 7-meter-diameter reusable rockets signals an ambitious push in their space capabilities. This move could intensify competition in the launch market, as nations and private companies alike scramble to keep pace.
